gaps.title: Zero local cache hit-rate measurement — the metric the harness tells itself to watch does not exist anywhere
gaps.detail: No script, statusline, report, or doctor check computes or displays cache_read/cache_creation tokens or a hit-rate. The statusline reads only model/cwd/cost/context fill. cost-report.sh aggregates only total_cost_usd from ccusage blocks and usage.jsonl, discarding any cache-token fields present in the captured JSON. The context-budget skill names 'Cache hit rate dropping' as its trigger condition, but nothing in the harness can produce that number — the trigger is mechanically unevaluatable. cache_read_tokens does flow to Langfuse via OTEL, but no in-repo report, alert, or dashboard consumes it, and Langfuse requires external setup (otelHeadersHelper reads ~/.config/langfuse/keys.env). RESEARCH.md even cites the tool that would fix this (claude-statusline-enhanced, 'cache hit rate visibility') but it is a catalogue citation, not installed or wired.
gaps.evidence: .claude/statuslines/budget.sh:13-17 extracts only model/current_dir/total_cost_usd/context tokens — no cache fields. .claude/scripts/cost-report.sh:46 `total=$(... | jq '[.[].total_cost_usd] | add // 0')` and :52-59 awk matches only "total_cost_usd" — cache token fields in usage.jsonl are dropped. .claude/skills/context-budget/SKILL.md:4 `when_to_use: Context >60% full. Cache hit rate dropping.` docs/OBSERVABILITY.md:57 (cache_read_tokens exported, never consumed in-repo). docs/RESEARCH.md:155 (uninstalled tool citation). grep for cache_hit/cache_read across .claude/ and docs/ matches only those three doc/skill files — no executable code.
gaps.recommendation: Extend cost-report.sh to also sum cacheReadInputTokens/cacheCreationInputTokens from the already-captured ccusage JSON and emit a hit_rate field into cost-summary.json; surface it in budget.sh statusline (e.g. 'cache:87%') and add a harness-doctor warning when hit-rate over the last day drops below a threshold. That makes context-budget's 'cache hit rate dropping' trigger actually evaluatable.
gaps.verdict_note: Every cited line verified. budget.sh:13-17 reads only model/current_dir/total_cost_usd/context tokens. cost-report.sh:46 jq-extracts only total_cost_usd from ccusage blocks; the awk fallback (:52-59) and per-agent attribution (:64-81) likewise match only total_cost_usd — cache token fields present in session-end.sh's raw ccusage capture (session-end.sh:49-56 appends raw blocks to usage.jsonl) are never consumed. Repo-wide grep for cache_read/cache_creation/cacheRead/cacheCreation/cache-hit/hit-rate across .claude/scripts, .claude/hooks, .claude/statuslines, .github returns zero executable hits; the only matches are context-budget/SKILL.md:4 (the trigger condition), docs/OBSERVABILITY.md:57 (OTEL export to external Langfuse), and docs/RESEARCH.md:155 (uninstalled tool citation). The context-budget skill body computes token costs via wc -c/4 but nothing cache-related (SKILL.md:24-30). The 'cache hit rate dropping' trigger is mechanically unevaluatable as claimed.

gaps.title: .claude/skills/* is the one §IX cache surface left unprotected by the constitution guard
gaps.detail: §IX explicitly names 'skill frontmatter' as a cache-stability surface, and skill descriptions load into the prefix every session (CLAUDE.md developer guide: 'Description (~100 tokens) loads into context at every session start'). The pre-edit-constitution-guard deny-list covers .claude/CLAUDE.md, settings.json, hooks/*, rules/*, agents/*, and .mcp.json — but has no .claude/skills/* entry. Combined with defaultMode acceptEdits (file edits auto-accepted) and no Edit/Write permission rule scoping .claude/skills, an agent can rewrite live SKILL.md frontmatter mid-run with no mechanical barrier, churning the next sessions' cached prefix. The memory.proposed promotion path mitigates the autonomous skill-creation route, but direct edits remain unguarded — an asymmetry given agents/* IS guarded.
gaps.evidence: .claude/hooks/pre-edit-constitution-guard.sh:81-93 — deny case list contains `.claude/agents/*` and `.claude/rules/*` but no `.claude/skills/*`. .claude/settings.json:27 `"defaultMode": "acceptEdits"`; allow list (:37-68) has no Edit(.claude/skills/**) entry either way. .claude/CLAUDE.md §IX names 'skill frontmatter' explicitly.
gaps.recommendation: Add `.claude/skills/*` to the pre-edit-constitution-guard deny case list (the FORCE_CONSTITUTION_EDIT escape hatch already covers legitimate operator edits and harness-development sessions), or at minimum add a PostToolUse warning when a live SKILL.md is edited mid-session.
gaps.verdict_note: Verified: pre-edit-constitution-guard.sh:81-93 deny case list covers .claude/CLAUDE.md, .claude/settings.json, .claude/hooks/*, .claude/rules/*, .claude/agents/*, .mcp.json, .github/workflows/*, .github/rulesets/*, .github/CODEOWNERS, tasks/TASKS.md, specs/active/* — no .claude/skills/* entry. settings.json:27 sets defaultMode acceptEdits, and neither the allow list (:37-253) nor the deny list (:276-351) contains any Edit/Write rule scoping .claude/skills. No other hook protects skills (pre-write-secret-scan is secrets-only). The asymmetry vs the guarded agents/* is real, and .claude/CLAUDE.md §IX explicitly names skill frontmatter as a cache-stability surface. Minor addition strengthening the gap: .claude/commands/* (legacy commands, also session-loaded descriptions) is equally unguarded.

gaps.title: Residual per-turn changing injections (dirty-file count; stuck-streak counter)
gaps.detail: Two injections change nearly every turn: the dirty-file count in user-prompt-context.sh, and during a stuck loop the short reminder 'still stuck (streak=$N)' whose integer increments each turn. Because UserPromptSubmit additionalContext is appended into the new user turn, these do NOT invalidate the existing cached prefix — but they are guaranteed-unique tokens written into the transcript every turn (each immediately becomes cache-creation rather than cache-read content), and the streak counter fires precisely during loops, the same condition Round 5 D5 was fixing. Cost is small (~15-25 tokens/turn); this is polish, not a hole.
gaps.evidence: .claude/hooks/user-prompt-context.sh:16,23 — `dirty=$(git status --porcelain | wc -l)` injected as '[harness] Branch: $branch | Dirty files: $dirty' every turn. .claude/hooks/workflow-state.sh:119-122 — `<warn>still stuck (streak=$streak); see BREAK-LOOP above</warn>` re-emitted with an incrementing number every stuck turn.
gaps.recommendation: Bucket the dirty count (clean/dirty or 0/1-9/10+) so the string is stable across most turns, and drop the streak integer from the repeat reminder ('still stuck; see BREAK-LOOP above').
gaps.verdict_note: Verified: user-prompt-context.sh:16 computes dirty=$(git status --porcelain | wc -l) and :23 injects '[harness] Branch: $branch | Dirty files: $dirty' as additionalContext every turn. workflow-state.sh:119-121 re-emits '<warn>still stuck (streak=$streak); see BREAK-LOOP above</warn>' with an incrementing integer on every stuck turn after the first warning — directly beneath the Round 5 D5 comment (:105-107) noting loops are 'exactly when the context cache is most valuable', so the residual changing integer does undercut that same fix's intent. The auditor correctly notes these are appended to new user turns and do not invalidate the cached prefix; this is accurately scoped as low-severity polish (~15-25 unique tokens/turn).

gaps.title: Dream lifecycle destroys pending skill proposals and candidates (shared .claude/memory.proposed/ directory)

The guard at lines 55-65 only skips when a *prior dream* set awaiting_review=true; proposals created by skill-creator or the detector alone do not set that flag, so they are silently deleted. (b) Conversely, /dream-review --approve (dream-review.md:48-49) does `rm -rf $CANONICAL; mv $PROPOSED $CANONICAL` — relocating un-reviewed skill proposals into .claude/memory/skills/, where --approve-skill's hardcoded path `.claude/memory.proposed/skills/$slug` (dream-review.md:66) can no longer find them. gaps.title: No enforcement of skill use — hints are advisory with no adherence signal
gaps.detail: Nothing mechanically requires that a relevant skill be invoked before starting a task. skill-router.sh:5-7 declares itself a hint overlay; the constitution mandates TDD/verification *outcomes* (verify.sh TDD ledger, §VII) but no hook checks that e.g. db-migration was consulted before writing a migration, or tdd-loop before implementing. gaps.title: No empty-backlog -> ideate trigger anywhere in the autonomous loops
gaps.detail: The headline capability of this dimension — 'once current features are done, auto-propose the next one' — has no mechanical trigger. Every autonomous loop treats an empty backlog as a terminal STOP, never as a hand-off to the (existing) proposal pipeline: loop-iteration.sh exits 1 on no pending tasks; verify-loop's first stop condition is 'No more unblocked tasks'; the overnight routine's stop list begins with the same. None of them chain to /feedback triage, roadmap-architect, /roadmap cut, or even a 'draft a proposal for human review' step. The entire feedback->triage->initiative->spec pipeline exists but is only ever entered by a human typing /feedback triage or /initiative create. The auto-dream-check Stop hook fires /dream (memory consolidation) but nothing analogous fires ideation.
gaps.evidence: .claude/scripts/loop-iteration.sh:53-56 ('STOP no pending tasks'; exit 1); .claude/skills/verify-loop/SKILL.md:37-44 (stop conditions: 'No more unblocked tasks in tasks/TASKS.md'); .claude/routines/overnight-build.yml:161-165 ('Stop when ANY of: No more unblocked tasks...'); .claude/commands/feedback.md:5 and .claude/commands/roadmap.md:5 both set disable-model-invocation: true (human-invoked only); grep for 'ideate|propose next|backlog' across dream/SKILL.md, auto-dream-check.sh, render-overnight-report.sh found nothing
gaps.recommendation: Add an 'idle branch' to the loop stop path: when loop-iteration.sh / the overnight prompt detect zero pending tasks, instead of exiting, run /feedback triage (or read _triage-latest.md) plus the OKR gap table and spawn roadmap-architect in plan mode to write a single proposal file (e.g. .claude/memory.proposed/next-feature-<date>.md or a draft spec with status: draft-autopilot-needs-review). Keep the human gate — propose, never auto-promote. Add the same branch to overnight-build.yml's END OF RUN section so the morning report contains 'backlog empty; proposed candidate X grounded in FB-### + KR-###'.
gaps.verdict_note: All cited evidence verified: loop-iteration.sh:52-56 logs 'STOP no pending tasks' and exits 1; verify-loop/SKILL.md:39 lists 'No more unblocked tasks in tasks/TASKS.md' as the first stop condition; overnight-build.yml:161-162 stops on 'No more unblocked tasks' and its END OF RUN (lines 183-191) runs only /dream + OVERNIGHT_REPORT + Slack ping. The entire proposal pipeline is human-gated: feedback.md:5, roadmap.md:5, okrs.md:5, and initiative.md:5 all set disable-model-invocation: true, so the model cannot self-invoke it. auto-dream-check.sh fires only /dream. Grep across hooks/scripts/routines for ideate/propose-next/backlog-empty hand-offs found nothing. The closest thing is feedback-extractor.md:55's advisory 'followup_tasks: /feedback triage if N >= 5' handoff line, which is not a trigger and is gated by disable-model-invocation anyway. Gap is real.

gaps.title: Triage — the actual ranking/proposal step — has no scheduled trigger and no deterministic scorer
gaps.detail: Intake is scheduled (feedback-poll.yml hourly) but triage, the step that converts raw FB entries into ranked candidates 'for /specify or /initiative create', is documented as 'Runs weekly + on-demand' yet no routine exists for it — the routines directory has feedback-poll, oq-aging, appetite-circuit-breaker, etc., but no feedback-triage.yml. The scoring itself (severity x ARR x renewal-proximity) is implemented as a free-text claude -p prompt, not a script — there is no deterministic scorer, no test, and nothing validate.sh checks in the feedback layer. So even with intake running, FB entries can accumulate in active/ indefinitely with nothing surfacing candidates.
gaps.evidence: .claude/commands/feedback.md:37 ('Runs weekly + on-demand') vs .claude/routines/ listing (no triage routine); feedback.md:129-130 (triage is 'claude -p --max-turns 20 --max-budget-usd 0.50 "Run feedback triage..."' — prompt-only); grep -i feedback .claude/scripts/validate.sh returned no matches
gaps.recommendation: Add a feedback-triage.yml weekly routine (or fold a triage step into the overnight prompt's END OF RUN), and extract the score into a small deterministic script (severity weight x arr_band weight x renewal-proximity decay) so the LLM clusters but the ranking is reproducible and testable.
gaps.verdict_note: Verified: .claude/routines/ contains feedback-poll, oq-aging, appetite-circuit-breaker, atlas-refresh, constitution-compact-cron, dream-cron, gc-nightly, hotfix-sentry-poll, overnight-build, quarterly-archive — no triage routine, despite feedback.md:37 documenting triage as 'Runs weekly + on-demand'. feedback-poll.yml:60-61 explicitly disclaims it: 'This routine ONLY records. It does not triage, score, or open specs/initiatives.' The scorer is a free-text prompt: feedback.md:129-130 is 'claude -p --max-turns 20 --max-budget-usd 0.50 "Run feedback triage... score by severity x ARR x renewal-proximity..."' — no script, no test. grep -iE 'feedback|triage' .claude/scripts/validate.sh: zero matches. Gap is real.

gaps.title: All feedback source connectors are disabled/unauthenticated out of the box, and the poll routine is a non-executable template
gaps.detail: The chain starts cold by default: feedback-poll.yml enables only the slack connector — fireflies, intercom, and pendo are commented out; the .mcp.json entries for those three servers auth via env vars that default to empty (${FIREFLIES_API_KEY:-} etc.), and the routine itself is a Cloud Routine template the operator must manually paste into claude.ai/code/routines — there is no local fallback (contrast: local-overnight-build.sh exists as a backstop for overnight-build.yml, but nothing equivalent exists for feedback-poll). Additionally, .claude/memory/feedback/ ships only 0000-template.md — the active/ and closed/ directories the pipeline writes to don't exist in the template (scripts tolerate this, but it signals the layer has never run). This is partially expected for a BYO template harness, but no doc/setup step prompts the operator to wire these sources, and harness checks don't surface 'feedback sources unwired'.

However they are unauthenticated by default (.mcp.json:303/315/327 — FIREFLIES_API_KEY/INTERCOM_ACCESS_TOKEN/PENDO_INTEGRATION_KEY all '${...:-}' empty-default), and feedback-poll.yml:34-39 enables only the slack connector with the other three commented out. The rest holds: feedback-poll.yml header (lines 1-10) says it is a Cloud Routine template the operator must configure; local-overnight-build.sh exists as the overnight backstop but no feedback equivalent exists in .claude/scripts/; .claude/memory/feedback/ contains only 0000-template.md (no active/ or closed/ dirs; post-ship-close-feedback.sh:23 tolerates the absence); grep for 'feedback' in setup.sh, harness-doctor.sh, harness-doctor.md, and docs/ADOPTION.md returned zero matches, and no doc outside research notes mentions wiring Fireflies/Intercom/Pendo. So the layer ships unwired and nothing surfaces that.

gaps.title: No automated revenue signal — ARR/renewal data is hand-entered or aspirational Pendo metadata; OKR 'Today' values are static text
gaps.detail: Prioritization is nominally revenue-driven (severity x ARR x renewal-proximity; P0 defined as 'imminent churn / revenue at risk'; OKR O2 is 'revenue protection') but no mechanism actually sources revenue data. arr_band and contract_renewal in FB frontmatter are typed by the extractor from 'Pendo's account-attached metadata' (Pendo unwired by default per the previous gap) or by a human via /feedback log. There is no billing/CRM integration in the active server set — Stripe is only a catalogue entry under _disabled_examples, and no Salesforce/HubSpot/recurring-revenue source exists anywhere in .mcp.json. The OKR 'Today' columns (e.g. checkout failure 1.7%, self-serve 51%) are static markdown numbers with no script that refreshes them from telemetry, so 'is the current feature done / did it move revenue' is unverifiable by the harness.

gaps.title: /okrs draft ignores the feedback registry; /feedback link clobbers existing refs
gaps.detail: Two small disconnects in the closed loop. (1) /okrs draft — the quarterly mechanism for proposing what to pursue next — lists its inputs as in-flight initiatives, incident themes, and sponsor asks, omitting .claude/memory/feedback/_triage-latest.md entirely, so accumulated customer signal does not feed next-quarter KR drafting. (2) /feedback link uses sed 's/^spec_refs:.*/spec_refs: [id]/' which overwrites the whole array rather than appending; an FB linked to a second spec loses the first link (the code comments acknowledge 'simplistic — proper YAML editor preferred'), weakening the spec<->feedback traceability that post-ship-close-feedback.sh depends on.
gaps.evidence: .claude/commands/okrs.md:30-36 (/okrs draft input list — no feedback mention); .claude/commands/feedback.md:147-148 (sed full-line replace with comment 'simplistic — proper YAML editor preferred'); .claude/scripts/post-ship-close-feedback.sh:32 (grep on spec_refs is the closure mechanism that loses entries if clobbered)
gaps.recommendation: Add 'Top themes from .claude/memory/feedback/_triage-latest.md' to /okrs draft's input list, and change /feedback link to append into the bracketed array (or use a 2-line awk) so multi-spec feedback keeps all refs.
gaps.verdict_note: Both halves verified. (1) okrs.md:30-35: '/okrs draft' inputs are 'Currently in-flight initiatives', 'Themes from recent incidents', 'Strategic asks from sponsors/execs' — no mention of .claude/memory/feedback/ or _triage-latest.md. (2) feedback.md:147-148: the comment says 'Append the target_id to the array' but the code is sed -i.bak -E "s/^${target_kind}:.*/${target_kind}: [${target_id}]/" — a full-line replace that drops any existing refs; the comment itself admits 'simplistic — proper YAML editor preferred'. post-ship-close-feedback.sh:32 greps '^spec_refs:.*' as the closure mechanism, so a clobbered ref silently breaks ship-time closure. Additionally, the documented 'bidirectional' linking (feedback.md:48 — adding feedback_refs to the spec) is not implemented in the sketch at all, making traceability slightly weaker than the gap stated.
